separation: The related LEA current transition, stationary torque grid, and thermal drive-cycle releases involve distinct acquisitions and lack a common test identifier. Do not join individual files across releases.
creator: Anian Brosch (Kaggle release author); related article by Anian Brosch, Oliver Wallscheid, and Joachim Böcker.
rights: Kaggle declares “Data files © Original Authors”. No explicit right to redistribute the source tables was verified. Only independently calculated aggregates, condition-level current summaries, differences of two measurements, model statistics, checksums and an independent reader are shared; no full source torque table or raw waveform is included.
query_log: Followed the public torque-characteristics link on the Electric Motor Temperature release to its distinct Kaggle family. API dataset listing identifies two independently compressed speed time series and a small torque table.

Followed the release’s detailed dataset description and IEEE 9359525. Compared release slug, article DOI and normalized titles with the project history. DataCite title/author searches did not yield a separate dataset DOI.

documentation.title: Data Set Description: Torque Characteristics of a Permanent Magnet Motor - 74 Million Samples for Data-Driven Learning
documentation.locators: Section III and Tables II–III. Stationary left-half id-iq operating grid, 0.5 s per point, phase currents and voltages at 1 MHz, angle, dc bus voltage and elementary state from control ADCs (20 kHz) placed on the 1 MHz grid. HBM T10FS 2 kN·m strain-gauge shaft transducer. The released torque is averaged per speed and operating point; bearing drag, friction, inertia and resonance separate shaft measurements from air-gap torque.

coverage.short_group: 2000 rpm OP 38 has 499,999 rows; all other groups have 500,000.
coverage.current_missing: 11 rows with incomplete phase currents in 2000 rpm, OP 5. All timestamps and angles available. Scope rows are counted even when omitted from current features.

processing: Read both single-member ZIPs to EOF and verify CRC. Use amplitude-invariant Clarke transform followed by d=cos(theta)*alpha+sin(theta)*beta, q=−sin(theta)*alpha+cos(theta)*beta. The features are group means of q and d*q (not the product of means). Pair the measured mean torque to (speed,OP) once. Fit an intercept and q, or an intercept, q and d*q, by unweighted OLS on all 74 operating points at one speed. Evaluate both the fitted speed and the held-out speed. Keep nominal time-grid variation, nonmonotone count and unavailable switching values visible.
results: Training at 120 rpm and testing at 2000 rpm, RMSE across 74 mean torque labels is 35.9410 N·m for q only and 13.6917 N·m with the d*q interaction; the within-speed values are 35.1630 and 13.2783 N·m. Reverse-speed transfer of the interaction model yields 13.3166 N·m.
limitations: The same operating grid is revisited at the second speed. Held-out speed does not imply new motor, new operating-point grid or transient torque validation. The affine empirical model and Park convention are declared baselines, not a reconstruction of the authors’ nonlinear model.

Only one mean strain-gauge reading per speed/point is retained. No transient torque, phase-resolved torque, commanded current history or clipping flag can be recovered from those means. Exceeding a nominal torque is not a saturation flag.
reproduce: Python >=3.11 with numpy and pandas. Store both source ZIPs as Time_series_120rpm.csv.zip and Time_series_2000rpm.csv.zip, plus Torque_Table.csv, in INPUT. OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python derive_torque_grid.py INPUT OUT.
